title_original: 《新婚美樂地》：鮮血，詛咒，與紅色的女巫
title_zh: 《新婚美樂地》：鮮血，詛咒，與紅色的女巫
summary_zh: 来源摘录：原文片名「Lali」在印地語有紅色之意，也有太陽的意思，既是表徵愛情、婚禮的顏色，同時也是薩朱的紅色胎記。紅色成為貫穿故事的顏色，祝福亦是詛咒，牽動著兩人的命運，但又不僅於此。在電影的詮釋中，紅色亦代表著令人窒息的傳統文化，街坊鄰居的耳語與視線，也來自父權社會長在薩朱的臉上，那一抹永遠未明的憤怒。 這篇文章 《新婚美樂地》：鮮血，詛咒，與紅色的女巫 最早出現於 釀電影 。
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "quote", "text": "撰文／許騰云 劇照提供／高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）、ifilm 傳影互動 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自古有訓：婚姻是神聖的結合，幸福的敲門磚。無論婚前是否相愛，只要踏入婚姻之門，社會必將傾力祝福──從此成為一對沐浴在愛情裡的幸福佳偶，然後美滿一生，嗎？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "婚姻歸根結底是糾纏人類數千年的結，長年擁護許多「正確的」社會價值觀，它是責任與情感的依歸，是建立家庭、繁衍後代的基石；同時也是隱性勞動最合理的遮羞布──在一場眾人見證的婚禮之後，權力的天秤往往開始傾斜，既是遮住一個人最為不堪、暴力的過往，也遮住另一個人無止盡地在婚姻制度內，周旋於情緒勞動、家務勞動的過程。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，婚姻又不僅擅於遮住事物，也將掀開他人未曾看過的一面：過剩的情慾、衝突、創傷、羞恥，包含婚前閉口不談的性，也因一紙證明而衍伸截然不同的意義。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat）多半圍繞著「愛情」的多重樣貌，並以喜劇結構暗渡巴基斯坦的傳統社會結構，進而探討社會文化、宗教等結構下的父權病灶。發表於 2022 年的 《愛情美樂地》（Joyland） ，透過鋒利、對比鮮明的鏡頭語言，將一對伴侶與跨性別者之間的糾葛，渲染成一場猩紅的家庭愛情悲劇。延續其導演風格，2026 年新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali）則進一步聚焦巴基斯坦社會的婚姻制度，推著命運的詛咒、精靈與惡魔，跟隨一場婚禮搖擺進場，以湧動的鮮豔色彩取代新人的愛情，編織一場沒有愛情基礎的婚姻鬼故事。", "links": [{"text": "《愛情美樂地》（Joyland）", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/films/6451d237fd8978000190ff0a/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "改編自導演親戚撰寫的短篇小說，《新婚美樂地》以古典寓言為架構，分為五個章節進行，從一場看似詭異卻又說不出其不尋常之處的婚禮切入： 人人歡欣鼓舞地，送一對佳偶攜手前往嶄新的人生階段，但喧鬧的傳統槍聲，卻更像吹起死亡與詛咒的號角──本該迎向天空的子彈，一槍打進了婆婆的腿，湧出的鮮血比新娘的鮮紅禮服更為豔人。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/e89a67GFm-_R3KHIb_CzEpV9lOehTNFObOdDfhLgPZM/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/e228950e-4a07-4fcb-96c6-ba39facedaa8.jpg", "alt": "《愛情美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：ifilm 傳影互動", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《愛情美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：ifilm 傳影互動"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "從電影開頭的五分鐘，庫薩特便宣示一場伴隨婚禮到來的腥風血雨，將如烏雲般籠罩家族全員。不久後，我們便會知道詛咒般的婚禮從何而來，美麗動人的少女席芭（Zeba），將嫁給臉上有著巨大胎記的「剩男」薩朱（Sajju），且他們原先並不認識。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "席芭身負命運詛咒，三次婚姻皆無果，深愛的伴侶更不知何故地，在婚禮前死於非命；薩朱似乎沒有太大的問題，但紅色胎記使他長年感到自卑，惟靠著母親的安排，才迎來人生第一場婚約──各自命運中流離的靈魂，碰在一起也未能擁有順遂的人生，壞事接二連三地發生，揮之不去的席芭詛咒為薩朱之母帶來死亡，家人也接連反目，關係亦危在旦夕。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "原文片名「Lali」在印地語有紅色之意，也有太陽的意思，既是表徵愛情、婚禮的顏色，同時也是薩朱的紅色胎記。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "紅色成為貫穿故事的顏色，祝福亦是詛咒，牽動著兩人的命運，但又不僅於此。在電影的詮釋中，紅色似乎擁有更廣泛的意涵，它代表著令人窒息的傳統文化，街坊鄰居的耳語與視線，也來自父權社會長在薩朱的臉上，那一抹永遠未明的憤怒。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最後，紅色成為燒向觀眾的豔火，直到所有人身負重傷，一地餘燼。不過有趣的是，紅色不只毀滅一切，卻又建立起女性的情誼。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/cvom4_2tTEn3Q2ylV0dYR9-dtLM-dmNaitLdifPFIQw/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/ebf491ff-4366-452d-bfb3-0b92c2f01398.jpg", "alt": "《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "婚禮過後，少女席芭入住新郎家屋，與丈夫、婆婆與智能障礙的隔壁鄰居玻莉（Polly）共同生活。薩朱的性情依然乖戾，對生活總是不耐與憤怒，但席芭意外地未受婆婆刁難，反而受到親生女兒般的寵愛，更成為薩朱母親傾訴心事的對象。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "關於席芭身上的詛咒，婆婆將之解釋為一種「過時的迷信」，同時還向席芭訴說，其實自己深愛的男人不是薩朱的父親。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當觀眾還沉浸在有些超現實的鄉村婚姻之中，婆婆的一番言論與自白直接戳破了故事本身所具備的古老質地，帶出了一種現代、理性的思維：女性的詛咒，是否純粹為父權文化所加諸的標籤？以及，傳統婚姻制度下的女人，能否愛著伴侶之外的人？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "婆媳之間的感情與對話，成為一道透光的細縫，使女人們發現自己不必依循社會成見，更不用透過彼此競爭、傷害以獲得家庭中的權力位置，女人可以在彼此的庇護下找到慰藉，進而尋回獨立思考的能力。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/g-SHWd7vSgG2VdWMLZjQg_rjvV15oLisSJaJ1Sz4aSg/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/af90733d-82ab-4e15-85f1-97ecea372f8f.png", "alt": "《新婚美樂地》電影海報／影像來源：IMDb", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《新婚美樂地》電影海報／影像來源：IMDb"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同時，當女人不再束縛於「傳統婆媳問題」，構成這份角力的父權結構，也就有了鬆動的可能──儘管對於席芭而言，隨著婆婆的驟逝，這段感情也僅僅只能是一道短暫的光。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "紅色，也是血的顏色。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在婆婆的喪禮後，席芭和薩朱突然長出了情慾的火花。男人夜夜探索妻子的身體，親吻她，佔有她，吸吮她，男人自身的苦楚，以婚姻之名找到了掩護。下一幕，觀眾看見席芭趴伏在廚房案前，隨後是婦科診所的診間，醫生交代：「休息一下，任何事過了頭都不好。包含愛也是。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "接著是，因為近期不能夠與席芭交歡，薩朱開始感到憤怒。 紅色，成了憤怒的顏色。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "長在薩朱臉上的自卑，鑽進他的心底而成了失語的野獸，即使在兩人的交往過程中，或許還能將之視為一種不自量力的沉默，但在步入婚姻之後，避而不談的習慣終究會成為問題本身。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "長期的沉默與自卑，導致薩朱沒有能力辨認自身的情感與價值，面對愛、失望、悲傷、困惑等情緒，他只能以極具攻擊性的憤怒，朝著身旁的所有女人發洩。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "薩朱選擇在自己的婚禮上緘默，也在母親的喪禮缺席，面對遲來的情慾、情感，他只是成為用陰莖說話的動物；直到面對周旋於席芭周遭的男人們，他認定妻子出軌，於是再也無法掩飾自己 ──憤怒、憤怒、憤怒！ 男人積累了一輩子的、無處宣洩的情緒，最後的選擇是將女人關進房裡，企圖搗毀她的身體，以作為自己失敗人生的陪葬品。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "男人對自己感到憤恨，也對妻子感到憤恨，更對社會充滿憤恨。 薩朱的恨意投射出同樣受父權遺毒侵害，卻丁點也不自知的男人們，於是男人們咆哮著一生的問題：為什麼自己活得那麼失敗？為什麼母親不愛父親？是不是母親眼中的我，永遠都不夠好？又為什麼，我得不到妻子的全部？"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/oAjNJdyZ-9q73gWvmD-4QvpERg_knFWqdDCUjqp3H2E/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/9aec773a-a5a2-43d7-a69b-f954dbb35e49.jpg", "alt": "《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影末尾，以一種近乎超現實的手法表現薩朱的癲狂，前段壓抑的恐怖元素至此全面釋放，他以一種非人的模樣披上紅色毛毯，喃喃將要化作精靈，要為薩朱（男人）的冤屈伸張正義。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "紅色毛毯包裹著生命的殤，與男人自卑、憤怒的心，也包裹住女人身體裡的一抹鮮紅，以及那一場早已脫軌的婚姻，紅毯從男人身上降到女人頭上，成為獻祭的頭紗，生命的詛咒一齊朝向谷底墜落。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當薩朱聲稱有精靈附身的紅毯披在席芭頭上時，紅色的憤怒反而成為勇氣的來源，成為女人奪回自主權的武器。此刻，女人終於在漫長的凌虐中，奪回敘事的權力，她步步逼近男人，說著：「今天我要剝除你所有的紅疤，所有污穢，你所有的毒和傲慢，還有你那空洞的男子氣慨。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "超現實的場景，甚至有些粗糙的荒誕手法，唐突卻有效地帶領觀眾進入另一層充滿惡魔、詛咒、精靈的魔幻世界，讓女人首度佔領此地，「真正地」成為女巫，披上紅色披風起身反抗。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同時，電影尾聲也再次為婚姻的古老寓言除魅，帶入更後設的現實，席芭不只是一場悲慘的命運、一段復仇的詛咒，而是女人的共同體：女人如何對抗浪漫愛裡的傳統父權想像，如何堅守生存的意志，毫不猶豫地灑脫？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "紅色，在遭火蛇吞噬後，會蛻變成什麼樣的顏色？"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/-7SUGiYtKaJZs1x-hCsyzvC4F9qpIH00nXlddo9eWN0/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/62d2f4d4-689c-40ca-b79b-2c8415194505.jpg", "alt": "《釀電影》熱天午後──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《釀電影》熱天午後──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "將於 2026 年 10 月 09 日正式開展的 2026 高雄電影節，以獨樹一格的選片視角與具爆發力的影像能量，持續撞擊當代觀影體驗的既定邊界。《釀電影》編輯室以「熱天午後」為策展專題，延伸自希臘導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）的短片代表作《雅典熱天午後》（Washingtonia，2014），連結柯薩瑪尼系列作品的城市、荒塚與冷酷異境。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次專題將由獨立評論人黃曦與導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）進行深度訪談，藉由系譜性地閱讀柯薩瑪尼，觀眾方能照見導演從植物、自然科學與傳頌百年的神話中，刺向當代社會的體制、階級、語言等困境，由此提出一道粉嫩且霓虹的提問；與此同時，本專題亦同步收錄獨立評論人沈怡昕於坎城影展現場，與柯薩瑪尼圍繞新作《人魚戀習曲》（Titanic Ocean，2026）之對答集。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本屆的「非典型視窗」單元片單，則集結 11 部來自世界各地的當代作品，此次專題將分別聚焦四部作品進行評論分析。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其中包括，獨立評論人許騰云剖析曾以《愛情美樂地》（Joyland，2022）獲該屆坎城影展「一種注目單元」評審團大獎的巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat），透過同為古典寓言的新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali），呈示喧騰、荒唐的禮讚與喪鐘，以及傳統婚姻制度下的女性宿命。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾任多年記者，現為文字工作者的阿潑（島嶼無風帶）帶領讀者走進韓國名導鄭智泳（정지영）新作《我的名字是⋯》（My Name），嘗試穿梭於當代校園、近代歷史之間，回顧被巨大歷史洪流所掩埋的「濟州四・三事件」（제주 4・3 사건）。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "獨立評論人蔡曉松則著眼改編自女籃球星烏莉安娜．謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova）真實故事、拉脫維亞導演維斯圖爾．凱里斯（Viesturs Kairišs）於新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）呈現的特異、詩意的鏡頭與表演呈現。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最後，由獨立評論人桑妮執筆法國邪典導演貝特朗．曼迪科（Bertrand Mandico）新作《羅馬瘋情畫》，探究一代名導如何攜手奧斯卡影后瑪莉詠．柯蒂亞（Marion Cotillard）與《燃燒女子的畫像》（Portrait de la jeune fille en feu，2019）諾耶米．梅蘭特（Noémie Merlant），在情色食人科幻狂想中，以鉛黃電影與費里尼式的怪誕拼貼，交出當代垃圾美學與女性主義謝幕的迷人花火。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
撰文／許騰云 劇照提供／高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）、ifilm 傳影互動 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

自古有訓：婚姻是神聖的結合，幸福的敲門磚。無論婚前是否相愛，只要踏入婚姻之門，社會必將傾力祝福──從此成為一對沐浴在愛情裡的幸福佳偶，然後美滿一生，嗎？

婚姻歸根結底是糾纏人類數千年的結，長年擁護許多「正確的」社會價值觀，它是責任與情感的依歸，是建立家庭、繁衍後代的基石；同時也是隱性勞動最合理的遮羞布──在一場眾人見證的婚禮之後，權力的天秤往往開始傾斜，既是遮住一個人最為不堪、暴力的過往，也遮住另一個人無止盡地在婚姻制度內，周旋於情緒勞動、家務勞動的過程。

然而，婚姻又不僅擅於遮住事物，也將掀開他人未曾看過的一面：過剩的情慾、衝突、創傷、羞恥，包含婚前閉口不談的性，也因一紙證明而衍伸截然不同的意義。

巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat）多半圍繞著「愛情」的多重樣貌，並以喜劇結構暗渡巴基斯坦的傳統社會結構，進而探討社會文化、宗教等結構下的父權病灶。發表於 2022 年的 《愛情美樂地》（Joyland） ，透過鋒利、對比鮮明的鏡頭語言，將一對伴侶與跨性別者之間的糾葛，渲染成一場猩紅的家庭愛情悲劇。延續其導演風格，2026 年新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali）則進一步聚焦巴基斯坦社會的婚姻制度，推著命運的詛咒、精靈與惡魔，跟隨一場婚禮搖擺進場，以湧動的鮮豔色彩取代新人的愛情，編織一場沒有愛情基礎的婚姻鬼故事。

改編自導演親戚撰寫的短篇小說，《新婚美樂地》以古典寓言為架構，分為五個章節進行，從一場看似詭異卻又說不出其不尋常之處的婚禮切入： 人人歡欣鼓舞地，送一對佳偶攜手前往嶄新的人生階段，但喧鬧的傳統槍聲，卻更像吹起死亡與詛咒的號角──本該迎向天空的子彈，一槍打進了婆婆的腿，湧出的鮮血比新娘的鮮紅禮服更為豔人。

《愛情美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：ifilm 傳影互動

從電影開頭的五分鐘，庫薩特便宣示一場伴隨婚禮到來的腥風血雨，將如烏雲般籠罩家族全員。不久後，我們便會知道詛咒般的婚禮從何而來，美麗動人的少女席芭（Zeba），將嫁給臉上有著巨大胎記的「剩男」薩朱（Sajju），且他們原先並不認識。

席芭身負命運詛咒，三次婚姻皆無果，深愛的伴侶更不知何故地，在婚禮前死於非命；薩朱似乎沒有太大的問題，但紅色胎記使他長年感到自卑，惟靠著母親的安排，才迎來人生第一場婚約──各自命運中流離的靈魂，碰在一起也未能擁有順遂的人生，壞事接二連三地發生，揮之不去的席芭詛咒為薩朱之母帶來死亡，家人也接連反目，關係亦危在旦夕。

原文片名「Lali」在印地語有紅色之意，也有太陽的意思，既是表徵愛情、婚禮的顏色，同時也是薩朱的紅色胎記。

紅色成為貫穿故事的顏色，祝福亦是詛咒，牽動著兩人的命運，但又不僅於此。在電影的詮釋中，紅色似乎擁有更廣泛的意涵，它代表著令人窒息的傳統文化，街坊鄰居的耳語與視線，也來自父權社會長在薩朱的臉上，那一抹永遠未明的憤怒。

最後，紅色成為燒向觀眾的豔火，直到所有人身負重傷，一地餘燼。不過有趣的是，紅色不只毀滅一切，卻又建立起女性的情誼。

《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）

婚禮過後，少女席芭入住新郎家屋，與丈夫、婆婆與智能障礙的隔壁鄰居玻莉（Polly）共同生活。薩朱的性情依然乖戾，對生活總是不耐與憤怒，但席芭意外地未受婆婆刁難，反而受到親生女兒般的寵愛，更成為薩朱母親傾訴心事的對象。

關於席芭身上的詛咒，婆婆將之解釋為一種「過時的迷信」，同時還向席芭訴說，其實自己深愛的男人不是薩朱的父親。

當觀眾還沉浸在有些超現實的鄉村婚姻之中，婆婆的一番言論與自白直接戳破了故事本身所具備的古老質地，帶出了一種現代、理性的思維：女性的詛咒，是否純粹為父權文化所加諸的標籤？以及，傳統婚姻制度下的女人，能否愛著伴侶之外的人？

婆媳之間的感情與對話，成為一道透光的細縫，使女人們發現自己不必依循社會成見，更不用透過彼此競爭、傷害以獲得家庭中的權力位置，女人可以在彼此的庇護下找到慰藉，進而尋回獨立思考的能力。

《新婚美樂地》電影海報／影像來源：IMDb

同時，當女人不再束縛於「傳統婆媳問題」，構成這份角力的父權結構，也就有了鬆動的可能──儘管對於席芭而言，隨著婆婆的驟逝，這段感情也僅僅只能是一道短暫的光。

紅色，也是血的顏色。

在婆婆的喪禮後，席芭和薩朱突然長出了情慾的火花。男人夜夜探索妻子的身體，親吻她，佔有她，吸吮她，男人自身的苦楚，以婚姻之名找到了掩護。下一幕，觀眾看見席芭趴伏在廚房案前，隨後是婦科診所的診間，醫生交代：「休息一下，任何事過了頭都不好。包含愛也是。」

接著是，因為近期不能夠與席芭交歡，薩朱開始感到憤怒。 紅色，成了憤怒的顏色。

長在薩朱臉上的自卑，鑽進他的心底而成了失語的野獸，即使在兩人的交往過程中，或許還能將之視為一種不自量力的沉默，但在步入婚姻之後，避而不談的習慣終究會成為問題本身。

長期的沉默與自卑，導致薩朱沒有能力辨認自身的情感與價值，面對愛、失望、悲傷、困惑等情緒，他只能以極具攻擊性的憤怒，朝著身旁的所有女人發洩。

薩朱選擇在自己的婚禮上緘默，也在母親的喪禮缺席，面對遲來的情慾、情感，他只是成為用陰莖說話的動物；直到面對周旋於席芭周遭的男人們，他認定妻子出軌，於是再也無法掩飾自己 ──憤怒、憤怒、憤怒！ 男人積累了一輩子的、無處宣洩的情緒，最後的選擇是將女人關進房裡，企圖搗毀她的身體，以作為自己失敗人生的陪葬品。

男人對自己感到憤恨，也對妻子感到憤恨，更對社會充滿憤恨。 薩朱的恨意投射出同樣受父權遺毒侵害，卻丁點也不自知的男人們，於是男人們咆哮著一生的問題：為什麼自己活得那麼失敗？為什麼母親不愛父親？是不是母親眼中的我，永遠都不夠好？又為什麼，我得不到妻子的全部？

《新美樂地》電影劇照／劇照提供：高雄電影節（© Khoosat Films）

電影末尾，以一種近乎超現實的手法表現薩朱的癲狂，前段壓抑的恐怖元素至此全面釋放，他以一種非人的模樣披上紅色毛毯，喃喃將要化作精靈，要為薩朱（男人）的冤屈伸張正義。

紅色毛毯包裹著生命的殤，與男人自卑、憤怒的心，也包裹住女人身體裡的一抹鮮紅，以及那一場早已脫軌的婚姻，紅毯從男人身上降到女人頭上，成為獻祭的頭紗，生命的詛咒一齊朝向谷底墜落。

當薩朱聲稱有精靈附身的紅毯披在席芭頭上時，紅色的憤怒反而成為勇氣的來源，成為女人奪回自主權的武器。此刻，女人終於在漫長的凌虐中，奪回敘事的權力，她步步逼近男人，說著：「今天我要剝除你所有的紅疤，所有污穢，你所有的毒和傲慢，還有你那空洞的男子氣慨。」

超現實的場景，甚至有些粗糙的荒誕手法，唐突卻有效地帶領觀眾進入另一層充滿惡魔、詛咒、精靈的魔幻世界，讓女人首度佔領此地，「真正地」成為女巫，披上紅色披風起身反抗。

同時，電影尾聲也再次為婚姻的古老寓言除魅，帶入更後設的現實，席芭不只是一場悲慘的命運、一段復仇的詛咒，而是女人的共同體：女人如何對抗浪漫愛裡的傳統父權想像，如何堅守生存的意志，毫不猶豫地灑脫？

紅色，在遭火蛇吞噬後，會蛻變成什麼樣的顏色？

《釀電影》熱天午後──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 高雄電影節專題／圖像提供：釀電影

將於 2026 年 10 月 09 日正式開展的 2026 高雄電影節，以獨樹一格的選片視角與具爆發力的影像能量，持續撞擊當代觀影體驗的既定邊界。《釀電影》編輯室以「熱天午後」為策展專題，延伸自希臘導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）的短片代表作《雅典熱天午後》（Washingtonia，2014），連結柯薩瑪尼系列作品的城市、荒塚與冷酷異境。

本次專題將由獨立評論人黃曦與導演康斯坦蒂娜．柯薩瑪尼（Konstantina Kotzamani）進行深度訪談，藉由系譜性地閱讀柯薩瑪尼，觀眾方能照見導演從植物、自然科學與傳頌百年的神話中，刺向當代社會的體制、階級、語言等困境，由此提出一道粉嫩且霓虹的提問；與此同時，本專題亦同步收錄獨立評論人沈怡昕於坎城影展現場，與柯薩瑪尼圍繞新作《人魚戀習曲》（Titanic Ocean，2026）之對答集。

在本屆的「非典型視窗」單元片單，則集結 11 部來自世界各地的當代作品，此次專題將分別聚焦四部作品進行評論分析。

其中包括，獨立評論人許騰云剖析曾以《愛情美樂地》（Joyland，2022）獲該屆坎城影展「一種注目單元」評審團大獎的巴基斯坦導演沙馬．蘇丹．庫薩特（Sarmad Sultan Khoosat），透過同為古典寓言的新作《新婚美樂地》（Lali），呈示喧騰、荒唐的禮讚與喪鐘，以及傳統婚姻制度下的女性宿命。

曾任多年記者，現為文字工作者的阿潑（島嶼無風帶）帶領讀者走進韓國名導鄭智泳（정지영）新作《我的名字是⋯》（My Name），嘗試穿梭於當代校園、近代歷史之間，回顧被巨大歷史洪流所掩埋的「濟州四・三事件」（제주 4・3 사건）。

獨立評論人蔡曉松則著眼改編自女籃球星烏莉安娜．謝米諾娃（Uļjana Semjonova）真實故事、拉脫維亞導演維斯圖爾．凱里斯（Viesturs Kairišs）於新作《女籃巨人烏莉亞》（Ulya）呈現的特異、詩意的鏡頭與表演呈現。

最後，由獨立評論人桑妮執筆法國邪典導演貝特朗．曼迪科（Bertrand Mandico）新作《羅馬瘋情畫》，探究一代名導如何攜手奧斯卡影后瑪莉詠．柯蒂亞（Marion Cotillard）與《燃燒女子的畫像》（Portrait de la jeune fille en feu，2019）諾耶米．梅蘭特（Noémie Merlant），在情色食人科幻狂想中，以鉛黃電影與費里尼式的怪誕拼貼，交出當代垃圾美學與女性主義謝幕的迷人花火。

此外，《釀電影》編輯室也將於影展期間走訪高雄電影節，進行其他短篇評論分析：「年度主題：抓馬人間」單元之《飛瀑怒潮》（Niagara，1953）、《夢魘人妻》（DreamQuil，2026）；「多倫多亞洲電影節精選」單元之《海草之家》（Seagrass，2023）、《世界上最ㄅㄧㄤˋ的國家》（The Greatest Country in the World，2019）；「抓馬跨世代單元：阿莫多瓦 vs 哈維爾雙人組」單元之《黑球》（The Black Ball，2026）；「大銀幕必看經典」單元之《深深腥紅 導演版》（Deep Crimson Director's Cut）；「耽美主義」單元之《青春抹世物語》（What We Saw）；「特別放映」單元之《1949》（Fatherland，2026）。

"“我从2018年开始接触苏联摄影档案。在早期的作品中，我感兴趣的是重复、碎片化、拆解和重新组合熟悉的母题——芭蕾舞演员、工人、士兵、政治领导人——以此探究它们最初的意识形态含义如何被削弱并置于新的语境中。在《许诺的蝴蝶》（Promoted Butterflies）中，我的焦点更直接地转向了政治权力和集体团结的影像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最初吸引我关注这些档案的是它们的视觉语言。我开始着迷于这些照片是如何被精心构筑的：身体、手势和表情的编排，重复出现的构图，以及每个元素似乎都在强化其他元素的严密性。尽管我使用的是苏联档案材料，但我的兴趣超越了那个特定的历史时刻。档案实际上是一个切入点，让我们得以思考更广泛的问题，即影像如何塑造集体认知、建构秩序与权威的观念，以及产生共同的信仰。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我所使用的照片描绘了精心编排的集体仪式，这是权力与社会理想化的外表。令我震惊的不仅是这些影像的流传有多么广泛，还在于它们彼此之间是多么高度相似。这种重复至关重要，因为它能营造出熟悉感。特定的视觉观念被不断重复，直到它们开始显得自然或不可避免。奇观让这些观念具有了情感上的说服力。政治权力通常通过这些视觉策略来运作，它不单单是告诉人们该想什么，而是塑造了现实本身被观看和体验的方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我将这些档案照片视为人造之物，视为通过重复、遗漏和视觉纪律构建起来的系统。我感兴趣的是创造一种情境，让这些无休止复制的政治仪式和集体团结的影像开始失去其稳定性。在《许诺的蝴蝶》（Promoted Butterflies）中，我引入了一个打断影像内部逻辑的元素，并揭示了这些系统实际上是多么脆弱。原本看似连贯、统一且受控的事物开始发生断裂。影像不再作为一个稳定的整体发挥作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Promised_Butterflies_2026_07.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Promised_Butterflies_2026_09.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "quote", "text": "“我希望原始照片与我的介入之间的张力保持可见，因为作品正是在这种碰撞中诞生的。我并没有在增加真相”——玛莎·斯维亚塔霍（Masha Sviatahor）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样难以捉摸的是，变革究竟是陷入了停滞、被无限期推迟，还是以一种扭曲的方式发生，从而催生出这些陌生的、不成比例的且令人不安的形体，让宏大的政治场景突然开始显得脆弱不堪。一条巨大的毛毛虫出现在党的观礼台上，让整个政治仪式感觉像是一场临时凑合、经过排练且充满戏剧性的表演。它几乎本身就变成了一种政治奇观的图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "让我感兴趣的是作品中运作的两种不同模式之间的碰撞。一方面是政治，它渴望控制、稳定和永恒；另一方面是有机事物，它遵循自身的逻辑，永远无法被完全控制。权力的影像往往包含着某种抗拒其自身内部秩序的东西。我引入的形态只是让这种抗拒变得显而易见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "标题《许诺的蝴蝶》（Promoted Butterflies）指向了所承诺的与最终兑现的之间的差距。在苏联的语境下，人们不断得到关于变革、进步和更光明未来的承诺。这些承诺通过意识形态、影像和集体仪式得以维持，然而，这种未来的表现形式与其实际体验之间总是存在着差异。变革确实发生了，但它从未与曾被承诺的乌托邦未来相吻合。变革未能兑现其自身的承诺。相反，它表现为一种模拟、扭曲或失败。承诺变成了未能实现的视觉建构。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种张力在今天同样显而易见。政治系统继续炮制着革新与进步的叙事，但问题在于这些叙事在实践中是如何具象化的，以及它们到底产生了什么样的现实。我们生活在一个往往无法被完全理解或控制的持续变革的时期。与此同时，我们似乎也处于一种漫长的期待状态中：等待战争结束，等待威权政权崩塌，等待暴力停息。这些变革被一次次推迟、打断，或是以扭曲的形式出现。变革从未完全顺应那些试图组织或收编它的系统。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Promised_Butterflies_2026_05.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Promised_Butterflies_2026_06.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "使用他人拍摄的照片不可避免地会引发关于署名权的问题，但对我而言，一切都始于档案本身。我所处理的影像并非中立的。它们被创造出来时就是意识形态的工具。它们不只是在记录世界，它们还在帮助塑造人们被鼓励去相信的东西以及对历史本身的理解。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我的角色并不是对这些图像宣示主权，也不是将它们抹去。我希望原照片与我的介入之间的张力能够清晰可见，因为作品正是在这种交锋中诞生的。我并不是在添加真理，而是创造了一个图层，让那些被排除或压抑的内容得以重现——不是以字面的方式，而是作为某种本不该出现的东西。我没有选择站在远处分析这些系统，而是对它们进行物理层面的介入，揭示出的并非宣传本身，而是它赖以运作并最终开始瓦解的机制。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些照片也改变了我对它们所处那个时期的看法。我主要使用的是《苏联摄影》（Sovetskoe Foto，曾是苏联唯一的摄影杂志，于1926年创立并在莫斯科出版）的档案，这些材料此前已在更广泛的意识形态框架内经过挑选、编辑和整理。渐渐地，我愈发注意到那些传达特定价值观的重复视觉结构。我对这些看似稳定的系统内部所掩盖的张力、矛盾和缺失产生了越来越浓厚的兴趣。档案馆不再是一个固定不变的历史记录，而是变成了一个可以被重新打开、质疑并进行不同解读的场域。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "mashasviatahor.com", "links": [{"text": "mashasviatahor.com", "url": "https://mashasviatahor.com/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.1854.photography/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Promised_Butterflies_2025_01.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "British Journal of Photography", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Masha Sviatahor is a Belarusian artist working with photography, archival materials, collage and photomontage. Her practice explores history, collective memory, and questions of power and ideology. Her first book, Everybody Dance! (2025), was published by TAMAKA. Her work has been exhibited at Yale University and Circulation(s) Festival, and she was named a BJP One to Watch in 2021. Here, she discusses her practice in her own words.

“I’ve been working with Soviet photographic archives since 2018. In my earlier works I was interested in repetition, fragmentation, dismantling and reassembling familiar motifs – ballerinas, workers, soldiers, political leaders – as a way of investigating how their original ideological meanings could be undermined and recontextualised. With Promised Butterflies , my focus shifted more directly towards images of political power and collective unity.

What first drew me to these archives was their visual language. I became fascinated by how carefully these photographs were constructed: the choreography of bodies, gestures and expressions, the recurring compositions, the precision with which every element seems to reinforce the others. Although I work with Soviet archival material, my interest extends beyond that particular historical moment. The archive is really a point of entry into broader questions about how images shape collective perception, construct ideas of order and authority, and produce shared belief.

The photographs I use depict carefully orchestrated collective rituals, an idealised façade of power and society. What struck me wasn’t only how widely these images circulated, but how strongly they resembled one another. That repetition is essential because it creates familiarity. Particular visual ideas are repeated until they begin to feel natural or inevitable. Spectacle makes those ideas emotionally persuasive. Political power often operates through these visual strategies, not simply by telling people what to think, but by shaping how reality itself is seen and experienced.

I approach these archival photographs as constructions, as systems built through repetition, omission and visual discipline. What interests me is creating a situation where these endlessly reproduced political ceremonies and images of collective unity begin to lose their stability. In Promised Butterflies I introduce an element that interrupts the internal logic of the image and reveals how vulnerable these systems actually are. Something that initially appears coherent, unified and controlled starts to fracture. The image no longer functions as a stable whole.

“I want the tension between the original photograph and my intervention to remain visible because the work emerges through that encounter. I’m not adding truth” – Masha Sviatahor

It’s also difficult to know whether transformation becomes stuck, whether it’s endlessly deferred, or whether it takes place in a distorted way, producing these alien, disproportionate and unsettling forms through which monumental political scenes suddenly begin to appear fragile. A giant caterpillar appearing on a party tribune makes the entire political ritual feel temporary, staged and theatrical. It almost becomes an image of political spectacle itself.

What interests me is the collision between two different modes operating within the work. On one side there is politics, with its aspiration towards control, stability and permanence. On the other there is the organic, which follows its own logic and can never be completely controlled. Images of power often contain something that resists their own internal order. The forms I introduce simply make that resistance visible.

The title Promised Butterflies points to the gap between what is promised and what is ultimately delivered. In the Soviet context there was a constant promise of change, progress and a brighter future. Those promises were sustained through ideology, images and collective rituals, yet there was always a discrepancy between how that future was represented and how it was actually experienced. Change certainly happened, but it never coincided with the utopian future that had been promised. Transformation failed to fulfil its own promise. Instead it appeared as simulation, distortion or failure. Promises became visual constructions that remained unrealised.

That tension feels equally present today. Political systems continue to produce narratives of renewal and progress, but the question is how those narratives materialise in practice and what kinds of realities they actually produce. We live in a period of continuous transformation that is often impossible to fully comprehend or control. At the same time, we seem to exist in a prolonged state of expectation; waiting for wars to end, for authoritarian regimes to collapse, for violence to cease. Those transformations are repeatedly postponed, interrupted or emerge in distorted forms. Transformation never fully conforms to the systems that seek to organise or appropriate it.

Working with photographs made by other people inevitably raises questions of authorship, but for me it begins with the archive itself. The images I work with are not neutral. They were created as instruments of ideology. They didn’t simply document the world, they helped shape what people were encouraged to believe and how history itself was understood.

My role isn’t to claim authority over those images or erase them. I want the tension between the original photograph and my intervention to remain visible because the work emerges through that encounter. I’m not adding truth. Instead I create a layer through which what has been excluded or suppressed can return – not literally, but as something that was never supposed to appear. Rather than analysing these systems from a distance, I intervene in them physically, revealing not propaganda itself, but the mechanisms through which it operates and eventually begins to break down.

These photographs also changed the way I think about the period they come from. I worked mainly with the archives of Sovetskoe Foto [at one time the only photography magazine in the Soviet Union, founded in 1926 and published in Moscow], material that had already been selected, edited and arranged within broader ideological frameworks. Gradually I became more aware of recurring visual structures through which particular values were communicated. I became increasingly interested in the tensions, inconsistencies and omissions concealed within these apparently stable systems. The archive stopped feeling like a fixed record of history and became something that could be reopened, questioned and read differently.”

title_original: Philadelphians to Vote on Permanent Arts and Culture Office on Election Day
editorial_title_zh: 费城选民将在选举日对设立常设艺术与文化办公室进行投票
editorial_excerpt_zh: 拟议的选票提案将确保该办公室免受行政更迭的影响。

Goode）建立以来，该办公室一直致力于向艺术家发放资助、管理公共艺术空间并在市内举办免费文化活动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，它也一直受到历任市长不同意图和政策的影响。如果该提案通过，将确保该办公室在市政府中拥有常设地位，并确立首席文化官这一职位，该职位目前由表演艺术家兼教育家瓦莱丽·V·盖伊（Valerie V. article_text:
News

Philadelphians to Vote on Permanent Arts and Culture Office on Election Day

The proposed ballot measure would ensure that the office is immune from administrative overhauls.

Wikimedia Commons ,

CC BY 4.0 )

Philadelphians can help establish a permanent arts and culture office in their city this Election Day, November 3.

The ballot measure would ensure that Creative Philadelphia, the name of the arts and culture office under Mayor Cherelle Parker, is immune to overhauls from current or future mayoral administrations. Since its establishment by Mayor Wilson W. Goode in 1984, the office has delivered grants to artists, managed public arts spaces, and operated free cultural events in the city.

Yet it has also been subject to the different whims and policies of a spate of mayors. If passed, the measure would ensure the office has a permanent standing in city government, along with the role of Chief Cultural Officer, a position currently held by performing artist and educator Valerie V. Gay.

"Theoretically, you could rescind the executive order and the legislation would cease to exist," Benjamin Wilcox, the communications director for Philadelphia Councilmember Isaiah Thomas, who proposed the ballot measure, told Hyperallergic in a phone interview. "This initiative would make the office permanent and install it in the city charter."

article_text:
Source: Edinburgh International Film Festival

‘Skintown’

EXCLUSIVE: Conic and Break Out Pictures have teamed up to acquire UK and Ireland rights to Skintown , winner of the Sean Connery Prize at this year’s Edinburgh International Film Festival.

Conic will handle distribution in England, Scotland and Wales, with Break Out Pictures distributing across the island of Ireland, with a theatrical release scheduled for early 2027. The rights were acquired from sales agent Visit Films.

Skintown is set during the summer of 1994, as Northern Ireland stands on the brink of the IRA ceasefire. Two best friends are determined to escape their hometown of Enniskillen, so become entangled in a reckless scheme to sell stolen drugs at a local rave.

Skintown is directed by Kieron J Walsh, adapted by Ciaran McMenamin from his own 2017 novel. The cast includes 2020 Screen Star of Tomorrow Jack Rowan , with Chris Walley, Jamie Lee O’Donnell and Hope Ikpoku Jnr.

It is produced by Yvonne Donohoe for Ireland’s Keeper Pictures and Brendan J. Byrne for the UK’s Cyprus Avenue Films, with Katie Holly and Walsh as executive producers. Backers on the film include Northern Ireland Screen, Fís Éireann/Screen Ireland, Coimisiún na Meán, RTÉ and BBC Northern Ireland.

Skintown had its world premiere in competition at Edinburgh International Film Festival in August, where it won the £50,000 Sean Connery Prize for Feature Filmmaking Excellence. It subsequently won the Hitchcock Audience Award for Best Feature Film at Dinard British and Irish Film Festival.

“The appetite for this wild ride in and out of 90s Northern Irish rave culture through the prism of the Troubles, seems to be there,” said Walsh, who said the “commitment and enthusiasm” of Conic and Break Out “is undeniable”.

article_text:
Francesco Bonami , a widely regarded curator whose achievements include curating the 2003 edition of the Venice Biennale, has been named artistic director of the GES-2 House of Culture, the Moscow art space sited across a river from the Kremlin.

Opened in 2021 , not long before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the 440,000-square-foot GES-2 House of Culture is run by the V-A-C Foundation, which was established by the Russian-Israeli billionaire collector Leonid Mikhelson . The owner of one of the largest natural gas providers in Russia not managed by the state, Mikhelson became one the first individuals to be sanctioned in the UK shortly after the war’s onset. He appeared on the ARTnews Top 200 Collectors list between 2013 and 2021.

Even before the conflict began, the GES-2 House of Culture faced controversy. Teresa Iarocci Mavica, the museum’s cofounder, resigned at the end of 2021 for reasons that were unclear at the time. Some speculated that Mikhelson was personally unhappy with a monumental Urs Fischer sculpture sited outside the museum. Others drew attention to the fact that Mavica had personally toured Vladimir Putin around the cultural complex, whose official reasoning was that the V-A-C’s Venice space required greater attention ahead of the 2022 Biennale.

Shortly after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Ragnar Kjartansson canceled performances of a new work staged at GES-2, saying, “It is not possible to have this work continue as this horror begins.”

Mavica, an Italian curator who gained Russian citizenship in 2019, was replaced by Alisa Prudnikova, the founder of the Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary Art. Prudnikova will now step aside for Bonami to take up the mantle, though she will continue to do curatorial work for the museum.

Bonami, who was born in Italy and holds US citizenship, is well-known internationally. In 1993, he organized the Venice Biennale’s “Aperto” section for emerging artists; a decade later, he organized the art festival’s entire main exhibition. He previously served in high-ranking posts at the Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo and the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, and has done editions of Manifesta, the Whitney Biennial, and the SITE Santa Fe International. (He previously wrote a column called “Ask a Curator” for ARTnews .)

He has previously done work for the V-A-C Foundation, organizing such shows as 2024’s “Square and Space: From Malevich to GES-2,” which he organized with Zelfira Tregulova, director of the Tretyakov Gallery.

Responding to the notion that Western curators should abstain from involvement in Russia’s art scene, Bonami told ARTnews in 2024, “Sorry, but the ethics of curating is a bullshit concept that I don’t indulge in. I could write a list of my colleagues who are collaborating with, to the say the least, ethically questionable people—but this is not the point … Sanctions are economic, not cultural. To sanction culture is a white crime that kills people’s souls.”

Of his future work for GES-2, Bonami said in a statement , “In my understanding, the role of Artistic Director is to catalyse artistic energy. Our common goal is to search for the best projects for GES-2. My experience should help with this.”
excerpt_original: Bonami previously defended working in Russia and called sanctions a "bullshit concept."

article_text:
Composer Hildur Guðnadóttir , who won an Oscar with “Joker,” is already deep into “ The Bell Jar .”

Sarah Polley ’s Sylvia Plath adaptation, which recently wrapped, will give pop icon Billie Eilish her first starring role, while offering the composer a new kind of creative partnership.

“[Working with a fellow Oscar-winning musician like Eilish] makes a huge difference,” Guðnadóttir tells Variety . “You know she understands the process that goes into writing music, so what you write can really resonate with her.”

Related Stories

James Austin Johnson's Trump Stops by 'SNL U.K.' for Meeting With Burnham and Zelenskyy: 'You Don't Have One Guy Who Can Play Trump?'

'Crystal Lake' Hits 1.3 Billion Minutes Watched in 11 Days, Becoming Peacock's No. 4 Scripted Debut Ever

Building on a relationship forged on 2022’s Oscar-winning “Women Talking,” Guðnadóttir joined Polley’s latest project early, writing themes the filmmaker could play on set. She was equally keen to connect with Eilish before the singer stepped in front of the camera.

“We talked about what we envisioned for the music, and how we could translate what Sylvia experiences into it,” Guðnadóttir says. “For me, the core of Plath’s writing is that she’s searching for identity. She keeps asking, ‘Who am I?’ and then uses her writing to understand that. Billie, Sarah and I have been exploring how we hear that, how to translate it into music, and what music Sylvia herself might have been listening to.”

Guðnadóttir calls the film a career highlight.

“It’s one of the most exciting projects I’ve ever done,” she says. “Sarah and I are good friends, so getting to tell this story with her is amazing. I think it’s one of the most amazing books ever written.”

“You can feel it in every word Sylvia Plath writes,” she continues. “This burning need and yearning to find herself through her writing. I’ve been reading a lot of her work, including her books, essays and poems, and it’s vast. People tend to remember the drama of her story, that she had mental health struggles and a sad end. But her writing is so full of life, creativity and energy, and that’s what people tend to forget. I really hope this film can bring that back to center and celebrate her magnificent way of living.”

Variety caught up with the composer at this year’s World Soundtrack Awards in Ghent, where she was guest of honor. Hours before her trip to Belgium, Guðnadóttir was still mixing “Enemies,” the Ari Aster-produced A24 thriller. Directed by Henry Dunham and starring Jeremy Allen White and Austin Butler, the Chicago-shot cop drama let her play with urban ambient sounds.

“I find it really interesting how the sounds of the city work with the film,” she says. “I’m working a lot with environmental textures and city sounds, and how they can relate to the film’s music. Listening is always at the heart, along with my curiosity.”

Guðnadóttir would also love to return to the “28 Years Later” franchise, whenever the next installment arrives . At the World Soundtrack Awards, she described the “nerve-wracking” experience of watching the first in the new series, scored by Young Fathers, after finishing her work on Nia DaCosta’s “ 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple .”

“I never got to hear a single note or see a single frame of [Danny Boyle’s ‘28 Years Later’] while I was working [on ‘The Bone Temple’],” she says.

“I kept asking whether we should have some connective tissue between the scores, but it was a deliberate decision to keep the two completely separate. So when part one came out, I went to the cinema with everyone else. I was sitting there thinking, ‘Please work together, please work together,’ because I had already delivered my part and couldn’t change a thing. It was funny, but nerve-wracking!”

The description could apply to the series as a whole.

“The amazing thing about these stories, and about [‘The Bone Temple’] in particular, is that they look very gory, aggressive and violent, but at the same time, they’re very human, soft and funny,” she says. “I think part two is hilarious. So the question was how could the music amplify that.”

DaCosta wanted strings, while Guðnadóttir sought to counter their ethereal quality with something more grounded. Taking the film’s title literally, she turned to an unlikely source for percussion.

“I have a friend who runs a hamburger place just outside of Berlin,” she explains. “She has a good relationship with her butcher, so I got a deal to take the leftover bones. All the percussion in the film is made from bones. The shoulder bones made interesting clapping percussion, and the bigger ones suited deeper beating percussion. The smaller ones were better suited to flutes.”

Bur first, she had to prepare her instruments.

“I do everything myself, and that includes boiling the bones,” Guðnadóttir says with a smile. “I’m very hands-on.”

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "DEADLINE：人工智能（A.I.）是最近的热门话题之一。你最近主演了一部使用 A.I. 的短片《The Ride》。我想你并不排斥参与使用 A.I. 的项目吧？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "普尔曼：我的风向标永远是 A.I. article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Ron Perlman is still man of action. The indefatigable Hellboy and Sons Of Anarchy star, now 76, has half a dozen films in production, and next year is aiming to play Hemingway in a new biopic set in Cuba and will co-star in the anticipated Sons Of Anarchy spinoff Legends .

A year on from Deadline announcing the launch of Perlman’s Asylm Studios banner, we caught up with the veteran actor (who made his screen debut almost 50 years ago) and the company’s co-founder Willie Morris about their indie slate and Perlman’s anticipated studio projects.

DEADLINE : Ron, we almost met at the Venice Film Festival last month. I gather you were at the festival with a new project of yours called Sedona, but it wasn’t in the official lineup…

Watch on Deadline

Related Stories

'Grey's Anatomy' EP On How Harry Shum Jr. Juggles Medical Drama & 'Dancing With The Stars' & If It Affects His Presence On ABC Show

'Line Of Fire' Gets Backup Script Order As Lisa Katz Talks NBC Fall Rollout, 'Newlyweds' Exit, 2027 Pilot Season, Peacock Strategy & 'Dungeon Crawler Carl'

RON PERLMAN : Yeah, that’s right. Willie can touch on that project specifically…

WILLIE MORRIS : We just kicked off a partnership with Google and 100 Zeros [Google’s JV with Range]. We recently launched a teaser for Sedona on our new YouTube channel and we used some of their tech to give it depth, so that you could view it with VR glasses or spatial glasses if you wanted to as an additive feature.

PERLMAN : Last year I got to know Google VP Jon Zepp [VP Partnerships, formerly Managing Director of Entertainment Content] after I did the Doug Liman immersive film Asteroid . So he invited us along to the festival where they were doing some work in the immersive section. To me, Venice symbolizes a connection that’s temporarily lost, because it symbolizes the glamor and scope and pageantry of the way we used to enjoy our cinema.

DEADLINE : It’s a great festival for sure…So Google put money into Sedona?

MORRIS : Google put some money into our indie project, which is in post, and then in return we used their technology to create spatial videos that’ll appear on some of their launch campaigns with the glasses. So they they wanted some spatial content and to support the arts, and we needed some funds to help get this little indie movie up and going.

PERLMAN : Sedona won’t be ready for close to a year. But Google has been helpful in the launch of our YouTube channel. I’ve been evolving with regards to the intersection of tech and Asylm Studios. Tech isn’t something you can run away from, but it is something you can use as an enhancement to exploring the human experience.

DEADLINE : A.I. has been one of the hot-button topics of late. You recently acted in a short called The Ride that used A.I. I take it you’re not against working on projects that use A.I.?

PERLMAN : My barometer will always be whether the AI. is the tail that’s wagging the dog. If it is, I’m not interested. I’m not interested in any technology that replaces the unique contribution of the human heart and the human soul, but I am fully bracing myself for a way to use these new technologies to our advantage. Asylm is a celebration of conventional filmmaking, and and an extension of the shoulders upon which we stand. But everything that we’ve done here at Asylm just came out of the blue. It was like a punch in the nose. It was like that with our first movie, Kodak Super XX and with Sedona , which are both in post-production.

We wanted to create an environment where artists, particularly filmmakers, could flourish and have an opportunity to spread their wings with very original contributions to what has always been an edgy, dangerous and original art form, which has lost its way because streaming has diminished the pageantry and the scope of the space that cinema once occupied. Ours is basically a mandate to go back and and create an environment where that can happen as a norm rather than as as an aberration. At Asylm, we will try to be as much of an old legacy studio where we not only produce, but we also want to market and distribute our own films. Theatrical is the engine upon which everything else is based and it’s an incredibly potent revenue stream.

We don’t have the infrastructure or the war chest yet to to do all of the things I’m describing, but the dream is to become a full strength studio where we we make the movie and we put the movie out and we control all facets of its life all the way down to its last stop, which happens to be home entertainment.

DEADLINE : Do you have backers or is the company funded by yourself?

PERLMAN : We are in the process of building the war chest, but we’re a way off accomplishing that. It takes time. We have two movies in post and two or three others in development, and a TV series and a documentary.

DEADLINE : We’ve previously covered Kodak Super XX with David Dastmalchian and Kelly Marie Tran. Tell us about Sedona. There’s not so much online about that one. Lili Simmons stars, right?

MORRIS : Lili Simmons, Israel Broussard, Nicholas Cirillo from Outer Banks , and Toby Sandman from Running Point . I joke that it’s The White Lotus on acid, but it’s about an actress who meets a very average guy, convinces him to come to Sedona for the weekend, and then her and her friends pretty much gaslight him for the entire weekend. It’s a bit of a fever dream psychological horror, and it’s very fun. Meanwhile, Kodal Super XX — which is likely to be called Super XX ultimately — is being submitted to festivals at the moment.

DEADLINE : What’s going into production next?

PERLMAN : I was recently filming in Ireland on Amazon MGM and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster’s horror movie Seasons . But for Asylm, it’s a foot race between two projects that we came to the party with. One is a Hemingway project, which has a look at Hemingway in his last couple of years, everything leading up to his suicide. It’s when he’s beginning to lose everything. That’s a project that’s very close to starting production. And then there’s a comedy called Auxiliary Man , which is a Tarantino-esque comedy, essentially because it’s a lot of white guys speaking ebonics, thinking they’re gangsters when they’re nothing but losers and bodies are dropping left and right, but you’re always realizing that you’re watching a comedy. It’s a crazy ass script, and that’s close to getting into production as well.

DEADLINE : It’s the centenary year of The Sun Also Rises’ publication, so there have been various Hemingway events globally. And I have covered other projects about Hemingway towards the end of his life. Would you play Hemingway and what sets this one apart?

PERLMAN : Asylm will produce. I’m playing Hemingway. I’m also co-directing the film with the celebrated Mexican DoP Gabriel Beristain, who is the guy who originally brought me to Cuba, and this is where I became infected with with this story and unable to get it out of my my psyche. After a decade, we’re finally going to make it very soon.

DEADLINE : I’ve always been a big fan of his work and like many, have been fascinated by his life. Even if he’s been more out of fashion in recent years for some of the ways he lived and thought …

PERLMAN : I don’t know a writer that doesn’t blurt that out. But we’re leaning into all of that. Look, he had a profound influence on the last century as an artist. And yet all of that was eclipsed by the man and how colorful and interesting he was. He caused a lot of debate and discussion, and he was polarizing. That’s what began to fascinate me. That and the fact that during his last years he he was at the vortex of the fall of Batista, the rise of Castro, and the wrath of J. Edgar Hoover.

DEADLINE : And he used to write standing up at an easel, right?

PERLMAN : He did, because he had back problems…

DEADLINE : Is this an original screenplay or based on a book?

PERLMAN : It was a story told to me by Cuban writer Enrique Cirules, who passed away a decade ago. He was obsessed with Hemingway and was his major biographer in Cuba, and had great access to parts of Hemingway’s life and psyche. The logline for the movie is ‘of all Hemingway’s mistresses, Cuba is the one that killed him’. So, when Enrique he told me the story about this perfect storm of Hemingway circling the drain, and then adding all of these political elements, all these psychological elements, all this paranoia where he thought J. Edgar Hoover was following him, which everybody thought was crazy at the time, but turned out to be true. It just was a story that I couldn’t get out of my mind.

DEADLINE : Is the Hemingway estate involved?

PERLMAN : The Hemingway estate is completely behind us. In fact, they’ve offered us his former home, the Finca Vigía, which is now a musem, for us to shoot in. We have the complete cooperation of many cultural players in Cuba. We have access to the La Bodeguita del Medio bar where he drank mojitos. We have access to the El Floridita bar, which he drank daiquiris in. We have access to the hotel Ambos Mundos where he wrote standing up, and he had two other rooms in the hotel that he had dalliances in. We have access to his famous boat Pilar. We have access to all of that.

DEADLINE : So what needs to happen next on the project?

PERLMAN : The dream was always to shoot it in Cuba. We’re figuring out if that’s possible. We have a backup plan to shoot in Spain if need be, but we’re hoping to make use of all these great places in Cuba.

DEADLINE : How does this fit with your schedule on Legends, the upcoming Sons of Anarchy spinoff?

PERLMAN : I’m trying to get Hemingway finished before we start filming Legends , which is slated to be sometime in March. I always wanted to film the Hemingway movie in January or February because it’s a little bit cooler in Havana, and after that it gets brutally hot and hard to wear prosthetics, which I obviously will do.

DEADLINE : How excited are you about Legends?

PERLMAN : I was blown away by what Charlie [Hunnam] was able to do there. I know how long he’s been floating this, and I know how hard it was to to get this boulder up the mountain, and the fact that he succeeded, and then the reaction on the internet was pretty singular. I don’t remember seeing anything that had more enthusiasm in terms of the way the world reacted to the news. We can’t wait to get back to work with with FX. John Landgraf, for me, was the greatest executive I’ve ever worked for because he has the the genius of an administrator, but the soul of an artist. The stories he has greenlit and made happen on his network I’ve never seen from an executive before.

DEADLINE : And you’ll be playing versions of yourself, right?

PERLMAN : Yeah. Believe me, having to audition for that was was humbling [laughs].

DEADLINE : Do you think Taylor Sheridan will be back for it? Your characters famously clashed in the first two seasons…

PERLMAN : Not over my dead body, motherfucker [laughs].

DEADLINE : You’ve read scripts?

PERLMAN : The only thing that’s been written so far is the pilot. Charlie is just assembling the writing room right now. When I get back, I’ll sit in and listen to things that are being bandied back and forth. But I’ve read a version of the pilot. I’m pretty sure it’ll evolve before we shoot in March in New Mexico.

DEADLINE : So it’s the same world and tone of Sons Of Anarchy or is it a departure?

PERLMAN : It’s both. It’s incredibly divergent initially, but it morphs into something that has the kind of outlaw danger aspect that Sons had.

DEADLINE : Sounds fun…And as for Asylm, will you be looking for investors in the company as you look to ramp up?

MORRIS : We haven’t officially gone our for a raise, but I think over the next couple months Ron and I will probably go down that path. We’ve been trying to figure out a way to bring industry figures in so that it’s not just traditional VCs and investors, but it’s more open to the people that we love.

DEADLINE : Finally, there’s always interest in your potential return to the Hellboy universe. Is that in any way possible? There have been non-studio/Guillermo Del Toro Hellboy movies since your last outing in the franchise 20 years ago…

PERLMAN : I’ve said so much about this and pissed off enough people, but I’ll say it again for you: the original movies were meant to be a trilogy. In Hellboy II , we left off at a very awkward moment where the Liz Sherman character is pregnant with twins, and none of the promises of Hellboy being summoned into existence to destroy the world has been addressed. That would all have been in the third film, and I’ll always advocate for the making of the third film. I’m not interested in doing any other version of Hellboy other than finishing the trilogy with Guillermo [Del Toro]. It would be so epic. Like a Greek epic. Hubris, hamartia, destiny, nature vs nurture, it would be such an adventure. I’m 76 now, and if he comes to me and I’m 86, we’ll still do the motherfucker.

DEADLINE : Do you still speak to Guillermo about doing it?

PERLMAN : No comment.

DEADLINE : Well, lot of fun things going on at Asylm and beyond.

PERLMAN : To borrow [and adapt] a phrase from Al Jolson, ‘you ain’t seen nothing yet’. We’re building a great thing at Asylm.

excerpt_original: EXCLUSIVE: Ron Perlman is still a man of action. The indefatigable Hellboy and Sons of Anarchy star, now 76, has half a dozen films in production, and next year is aiming to play Ernest Hemingway in a new biopic set in Cuba and will co-star in the anticipated Sons of Anarchy…

title_original: Thomas Savary: At the Salers’ Pace
editorial_title_zh: 托马斯·萨瓦里：以萨莱尔牛的步伐
editorial_excerpt_zh: 每年五月底，法国康塔尔地区的阿朗什小镇都会将萨莱尔牛群护送到高山牧场。托马斯·萨瓦里（Thomas Savary）带着一台适马 fp 相机在那里拍摄了夏牧节（Fête de l'Estive），追寻着代代相传的手势与动作……

article_text:
Here, the cow is set in stone. On the Place du Cézallier, a cow and her calf carved from lava have watched over Allanche since 1996, placid sentinels of a town of some 770 souls perched at 1,100 meters (plenty of fresh air to go around). The rest of the year, the little basalt town moves at the slow pace of the plateau. At the end of May, everything tips over. Bells, hooves, brass bands, the smell of aligot and fritters: nearly 40,000 visitors come up to greet the herds bound for the summer pastures, and the village dreams of being a capital. Capital of what? Of transhumance, of truffade, of time that passes without passing. Thomas Savary went up quietly, to follow what is handed down from one hand to the next. A matter of horns and heart.

Photographer Thomas Savary did not come alone. In May 2025, Vincent Pietri, a longtime friend based in Aurillac, proposed, together with Allanche’s town hall, to tell the story of the festival through four different eyes. With Jérémy Laurichesse and Roméo Ichard, they covered both days of the Estive. “Between truffade and aligot, we roamed the event, photographing the herds as well as local crafts, the breeders, the residents and the public,” he recalls. The images found a first audience at the Regards en Cézallier festival, then during a five-day residency at Artopia, the cultural venue Vincent Pietri developed in Aurillac. A traveling exhibition came out of it. It circulated among local partners, from a car dealership to the departmental council.

Thomas set his rule from the start: no stolen pictures. “I never hid the fact that I was taking pictures,” he says. The camera, a Sigma fp chosen for its discreet size, served first of all to start conversations, to ask questions, to understand who does what. “Photography then became less an end in itself than a pretext for creating a connection,” he continues. He showed the screen to the people he had just photographed, and sometimes took down their contact details to send them the images later. The support of the town hall, and especially of mayor Philippe Rosseel, opened the breeders’ doors to him.

Thomas Savary often tightens the frame down to the detail, in a series made up exclusively of vertical images: two hands crossed on a shepherd’s staff, a scarf held by a small wooden clog. The device is familiar, and it has its limits. With so many fragments, the series at times verges on rustic imagery, a catalog of accessories. Yet here it serves a precise purpose. By leaving out faces, the photographer shifts the portrait toward the tool and the garment, in other words toward what is passed on. It is in these tight images that his statement on heritage finds its clearest form.

And then there is the child. Straight bangs, a hoodie printed with cartoon puppies, he brushes an animal’s flank with a sure hand and stares into the lens, brow furrowed, as if interrupted at work. Behind him, out of focus, an adult stands with arms crossed. “I’m thinking in particular of the photograph of this child with his brush, reproducing a gesture that his great-grandfather probably made before him,” Thomas Savary explains. The gesture is old; the hoodie is new. “It’s precisely this contrast that interests me,” he adds. On one side, gestures that cross the generations unchanged; on the other, thoroughly contemporary habits. The Estive, as the artist puts it, becomes the place where these two timeframes coexist.

The animals, then, get their own portraits. A cow faces the camera head-on, horns spread like handlebars, two yellow tags on her ears marked 6659. A thread of drool hangs from her muzzle. Neither endearing nor threatening, she is simply a presence. Thomas Savary remembers a breeder showing him a bull that had won a prize at the Paris Salon de l’Agriculture, and “the love and pride with which he spoke about his work, his skills and his animals.” Facing an animal that can weigh more than a ton, he describes “a mix of excitement, admiration and, I must admit, a little fear.”

On Sunday morning, the festival sets off. The breeders drive their herds from Allanche to Pradiers, a four- to five-hour walk, and the crowd follows. In an image taken from a distance, under a heavy sky, the procession is nothing more than a line of colors, anoraks and backpacks, running along the road at the foot of a hill, between the power poles. “There is something almost timeless about this ascent, at once deeply traditional and incredibly alive,” says the photographer. Higher up, a dry-stone buron (a shepherd’s hut) roofed with sheet metal hunkers down in the grass, yellow flowers in the foreground. And finally, on the ridge, a herd grazes in single file, barely bigger than grains of rice. That too is the Estive: what remains once the festival has passed.

Honestly, the series changed shape quite a bit with Sigma. The Japanese company has been producing very high-end equipment for some years, and Thomas Savary shared his images with the brand whose camera he uses. Sigma, present in Arles this year for the sixth consecutive year, offered him a show in the Off program during the opening week of the Rencontres de la photographie 2026. Shortly before, from January to June, he reworked the edit with Sigma’s teams and independent curator Audrey Hoareau, thought through the scenography, and prepared a book. The title tightened: “L’Estive” (The Summer Pasture). From July 6 to 12, on Rue du Pont, the prints were pasted on the wall and accompanied by a soundtrack of three minutes and thirty-six seconds by the photographer.

On October 11, Thomas Savary looks back on the whole project at the Salon Photo & Vidéo, the new name of the Salon de la Photo, at the Grande Halle de la Villette in Paris. In Sigma’s Rencontres space, he retraces the path from shooting with the fp to the hanging in Arles. In Allanche as in Arles, he says, the response was warm. The 35th Fête de l’Estive is scheduled for May 22 and 23, 2027, in Allanche.

Thomas Savary presents “L’Estive” on Sunday October 11, 2026, in Sigma’s Rencontres space at the Salon Photo & Vidéo, held October 8 to 11, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., at the Grande Halle de la Villette in Paris. Sigma is offering free tickets with the code SIGMA26 on sigma-photo.fr . More of the photographer’s work is on his website .

title_original: コトバの重なる場所
editorial_excerpt_zh: 国立国际美术馆将举办特别展览「话语交汇之处」，利用本馆收藏。随着翻译应用程序功能的提升，现代人可以轻松处理多种语言。不仅限于母语，人们可以轻松创作流畅的文章，语言障碍在跨文化理解中显著降低。然而，语言不仅仅是沟通的工具。它在漫长的历史中塑造了文化和艺术。同时，我们每天遇到的词语也培养和改变着我们的思维和意识。当拥有不同「话语」的群体和人们相遇时，这种接触可能带来积极的发现和变化，但也可能反复产生冲突、对立、支配和压迫等不对称关系。本次展览聚焦于亚洲被视为边界地带的地区，呈现围绕语言、民族、文化、意识形态交错场所的影像、图像和文字作品。艺术家们通过揭示土地的历史、生活在那里的人们的经历和记忆，展现出殖民统治和战争带来的分裂，以及规范性语言和意识形态压迫等现代现象。同时，也让人想象那些从公共记录中遗漏的人们内心的状态。现代艺术也是我们深入思考所处时代的批判性实践。希望本次展览能通过作品，深入观察历史的层次，激发对不同话语他者的想象力。

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "国立国際美術館では、当館コレクションを活用した特別展「コトバの重なる場所」を開催いたします。 翻訳アプリの機能向上により、複数の言語を容易に扱うことができるようになった現代。母語に限らず、なめらかな文章を簡単に生み出すことが可能になり、異文化理解における言語の障壁は格段に下がりつつあるように見えます。 しかし、言語／言葉は、単なる意思疎通の道具に留まりません。それは、長い時間をかけて文化や芸術をかたちづくってきました。また、日々出会う言葉によって、私たちの思考と意識は培われ変容していきます。そして、異質な「コトバ」を持つ集団や人々が対峙するとき、その接触がポジティブな発見や変化を導くこともあれば、衝突や対立、支配や抑圧といった非対称な関係が繰り返し生じてきたことも忘れることはできません。 本展で紹介するのは、アジアにおいて境界地帯とされてきた場所を中心に、言語や民族、文化、イデオロギーの交錯する場所にまつわる映像やイメージ、言葉に焦点を当てる作品です。土地の歴史や、その地に生きる人々の経験や記憶を照らし出す作家たちの実践は、植民地支配や戦争がもたらす分断、規範的言語やイデオロギーによる抑圧といった近現代の諸相を浮かびあがらせます。そして、公的な記録からはこぼれ落ちてきた、人々の心のありようを想像させます。 現代美術は、私たちの生きる時代をより深く考えるための批評的な実践でもあります。本展が、作品を通して歴史の地層を見つめ、「コトバ」の違う他者への想像力を喚起する機会となれば幸いです。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
国立国際美術館では、当館コレクションを活用した特別展「コトバの重なる場所」を開催いたします。 翻訳アプリの機能向上により、複数の言語を容易に扱うことができるようになった現代。母語に限らず、なめらかな文章を簡単に生み出すことが可能になり、異文化理解における言語の障壁は格段に下がりつつあるように見えます。 しかし、言語／言葉は、単なる意思疎通の道具に留まりません。それは、長い時間をかけて文化や芸術をかたちづくってきました。また、日々出会う言葉によって、私たちの思考と意識は培われ変容していきます。そして、異質な「コトバ」を持つ集団や人々が対峙するとき、その接触がポジティブな発見や変化を導くこともあれば、衝突や対立、支配や抑圧といった非対称な関係が繰り返し生じてきたことも忘れることはできません。 本展で紹介するのは、アジアにおいて境界地帯とされてきた場所を中心に、言語や民族、文化、イデオロギーの交錯する場所にまつわる映像やイメージ、言葉に焦点を当てる作品です。土地の歴史や、その地に生きる人々の経験や記憶を照らし出す作家たちの実践は、植民地支配や戦争がもたらす分断、規範的言語やイデオロギーによる抑圧といった近現代の諸相を浮かびあがらせます。そして、公的な記録からはこぼれ落ちてきた、人々の心のありようを想像させます。 現代美術は、私たちの生きる時代をより深く考えるための批評的な実践でもあります。本展が、作品を通して歴史の地層を見つめ、「コトバ」の違う他者への想像力を喚起する機会となれば幸いです。

出品作家：平敷兼七、下道基行、ツァオ・フェイ、前田藤四郎、村岡三郎、山城知佳子、上原沙也加、小泉明郎、イリヤ・カバコフ、北島敬三、ナタリア・パパエヴァ、ムン・キョンウォン＆チョン・ジュン、竹川宣彰、今津景、ホー・ルイアン、キャリー・ヤマオカ

editorial_title_zh: 彼得·纳吉逝世：横跨纽约与新德里的艺术家兼画廊主传奇
editorial_excerpt_zh: 后观念艺术家、Nature Morte画廊创始人彼得·纳吉（Peter Nagy）于67岁逝世。作为连接20世纪80年代纽约与当代印度艺术的关键人物，本文报道了其生平。本文来源：È morto Peter Nagy: storia di un artista gallerista tra New York e New Delhi...

"paragraph", "text": "在意大利，他的名字相对鲜为人知，但在英语世界尤其是亚洲，纳吉是一位举足轻重的人物。Nature Morte画廊缅怀他是一个“无畏、叛逆且极度自由”的存在，并强调了他对陈规旧俗的厌恶以及他与艺术家建立持久关系的与生俱来的能力。画廊还表示，根据他的明确遗愿，画廊空间将继续开放，原定的展览也将继续进行。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/peter-nagy-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "彼得·纳吉，《娱乐抹杀历史》，展览现场，Deitch Project，纽约，2020年，摄影：Genevieve Hanson", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "从20世纪80年代的纽约开始", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纳吉1959年出生于康涅狄格州布里奇波特，曾在纽约帕森斯设计学院（Parsors School of Design）学习传播设计，并在那里接受了艺术史训练。20世纪80年代初，他开始发展一种后观念艺术实践，该实践与图像复制过程、平面设计、广告以及商业品牌日益强烈的侵入性紧密相连。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他那时期的作品融合了拼贴画、艺术书籍中的图像、平面图、标志以及广告材料，通常经过连续的静电复印（Xerox）处理。复制成了作品本身的主题：纳吉对图像在被复制、降质、放大并逐渐剥离原始信息时发生的变化很感兴趣。在诸如《国际调查公寓》（International Survey Condominiums）等系列作品中，艺术史的年表与博物馆的平面图相互叠加，对艺术被组织、分类并转化为系统的机制提出了质疑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/peter-nagy-6.jpg", "alt": "彼得·纳吉，《娱乐抹杀历史》，展览现场，Deitch Project，纽约，2020年，摄影：Genevieve Hanson", "caption": "彼得·纳吉，《娱乐抹杀历史》，展览现场，Deitch Project，纽约，2020年，摄影：Genevieve Hanson", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在20世纪80年代，他的作品与当时将挪用、可复制性以及对作者身份的批判作为主要手段的美国艺术浪潮展开了对话。他通过群体材料（Group Material）参与了1985年惠特尼双年展，并于1987年入选卡塞尔文献展第8届。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Nature Morte与东村", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在进行个人艺术探索的同时，纳吉于1982年与艺术家艾伦·贝尔切（Alan Belcher）在纽约东村（East Village）共同创立了Nature article_text:
È morto il 13 ottobre 2026, all’età di 67 anni, Peter Nagy , artista, curatore e gallerista statunitense che ha attraversato due stagioni molto diverse dell’arte contemporanea: la New York post-concettuale degli anni Ottanta e, dagli anni Novanta in poi, la costruzione di una nuova visibilità internazionale per la scena artistica indiana. La notizia della scomparsa, avvenuta dopo una lunga malattia, è stata comunicata da Nature Morte , la galleria da lui fondata e diretta, con sedi a New Delhi e Mumbai.

In Italia il suo nome è relativamente poco conosciuto ma nell’area anglofona e soprattutto in Asia Nagy è stato una figura di primo piano. Nature Morte lo ha ricordato come una presenza «Senza paura, irriverente e selvaggiamente libera», sottolineando la sua insofferenza per le convenzioni ma anche la sua innata abilità nel costruire relazioni durature con gli artisti. La galleria ha inoltre fatto sapere che, secondo una sua precisa volontà, gli spazi resteranno aperti e le mostre in programma proseguiranno.

Dalla New York degli anni Ottanta

Nato nel 1959 a Bridgeport, nel Connecticut, Nagy studiò communication design alla Parsons School of Design di New York, dove si formò anche in storia dell’arte. Nei primi anni Ottanta iniziò a sviluppare una pratica post-concettuale fortemente legata ai processi di riproduzione delle immagini, alla grafica, alla pubblicità e alla crescente invasività dei marchi commerciali.

Le sue opere di quel periodo mescolavano collage, immagini tratte da libri d’arte, planimetrie, loghi e materiali pubblicitari, spesso sottoposti a successive riproduzioni Xerox. La copia diventava il tema stesso del lavoro: Nagy si interessava a ciò che accadeva all’immagine quando veniva replicata, degradata, ingrandita e privata progressivamente dell’informazione originaria. In serie come International Survey Condominiums , le cronologie della storia dell’arte venivano sovrapposte alle planimetrie dei musei, mettendo in discussione i meccanismi attraverso cui l’arte viene organizzata, classificata e trasformata in sistema.

Negli anni Ottanta il suo lavoro entrò così in dialogo con quella stagione americana che aveva fatto dell’appropriazione, della riproducibilità e della critica all’autorialità alcuni dei propri strumenti principali. Partecipò alla Whitney Biennial del 1985 attraverso Group Material e arrivò anche a Documenta 8, nel 1987.

Nature Morte e l’East Village

Parallelamente alla propria ricerca, nel 1982 Nagy fondò insieme all’artista Alan Belcher la Gallery Nature Morte nell’East Village di New York. Lo spazio rimase attivo fino al 1988 e divenne uno dei luoghi emblematici di una scena che cercava alternative tanto all’establishment di SoHo quanto al sistema delle gallerie uptown.

Nature Morte combinava sensibilità concettuale, cultura pop e attenzione ai meccanismi del mercato. Vi esposero, in fasi iniziali delle loro carriere, artisti come Steven Parrino , Gretchen Bender , Cady Noland , Louise Lawler , Sherrie Levine e Robert Gober . La galleria contribuì così alla definizione di un clima in cui l’opera non poteva più essere separata dai dispositivi di circolazione, promozione e consumo che la circondavano.

Questa doppia identità di artista e dealer accompagnò Nagy per tutta la vita. Non la percepiva come una contraddizione, quanto come un punto di osservazione privilegiato sul modo in cui produzione artistica, mercato, media e costruzione delle reputazioni si intrecciano.

Il trasferimento in India

Il passaggio decisivo arrivò nel 1992, quando Nagy si trasferì a New Delhi. Cinque anni dopo, nel 1997, riaprì Nature Morte nella capitale indiana, trasportando in un contesto molto diverso l’esperienza accumulata nella New York degli anni Ottanta. In un sistema allora ancora fortemente concentrato sulla pittura, Nagy portò un modello fondato sulla sperimentazione, sul rigore curatoriale e su un rapporto continuativo con gli artisti. Nature Morte iniziò a sostenere pratiche concettuali, installative, fotografiche, scultoree e legate ai nuovi media, contribuendo a connettere la produzione indiana con il circuito internazionale.

Nel corso degli anni Nagy ha lavorato con alcuni dei nomi destinati a diventare centrali nell’arte contemporanea indiana, tra cui Subodh Gupta , Bharti Kher , Jitish Kallat , Mrinalini Mukherjee e L. N. Tallur .

Negli ultimi anni Nature Morte ha ulteriormente ampliato la propria presenza. Nel 2024 è stato aperto uno spazio a Mumbai, mentre nell’agosto 2026 la galleria ha inaugurato una nuova sede permanente a Gulmohar Park, a New Delhi.

Proprio qui Nagy aveva curato The Evolution of the Soothsayer , grande progetto in due parti dedicato ai trent’anni della galleria in India e costruito attraverso circa 35 artisti del suo percorso storico. La seconda parte è in programma dal 22 ottobre al 12 dicembre 2026.

L’artista dietro il gallerista

Con il tempo, il successo di Nature Morte ha in parte oscurato la produzione artistica di Nagy, che tuttavia non si è mai interrotta. Dopo le opere in bianco e nero degli anni Ottanta, il suo lavoro si è aperto a pittura, installazione e linguaggi più ornamentali, con riferimenti barocchi, rococò e orientalisti.

Nel 2020 Jeffrey Deitch gli ha dedicato a New York Entertainment Erases History , mostra realizzata in collaborazione con Magenta Plains che ha contribuito a riaccendere l’attenzione critica sulla sua produzione. Le sue opere sono entrate nelle collezioni di istituzioni come Whitney Museum, Metropolitan Museum of Art e Museum of Contemporary Art di Los Angeles.

article_text:
Jonathan Davies’ article ( Abide with me: English choral music is a living part of our cultural heritage – we should cherish it, 7 October ) speaks beautifully to the contribution of English choral music to our living cultural heritage, highlighting the importance of cathedral choirs in particular, in giving children access to “world-class musical training, extraordinary cultural experiences and educational opportunities that might otherwise be beyond their reach”.

What he misses however, is just how under threat these bastions of England’s religious, cultural and spiritual heritage actually are.

Despite recent research from the Theos thinktank suggesting 74% of adults in England have visited a cathedral over the last three years, 80% of cathedrals in England are now in structural deficit. Several have recently reached crisis point, including those in Peterborough and St Davids . One in four cathedrals in England is now charging for entry, and even after significantly diversifying their income portfolios (including through controversial silent discos ), they continue to struggle.

More than 90% of visitors surveyed by Theos (including 94% of non-religious visitors) thought of cathedrals as a hub for community life, and the same number see them as a symbol of local identity and a way to connect with history and tradition. Despite their significant social and cultural contributions to communities, and being some of our oldest and most historically significant buildings (two are Unesco world heritage sites and many are almost 1,000 years old), cathedrals receive no secure state funding and limited contributions from central church authorities. Unlike museums and galleries offering free admission, cathedrals are also not subject to the same VAT exemptions on repairs or maintenance.

This has left many cathedrals crumbling, and their finances with them. Without cathedrals, English choral music would cease to exist. If more is not done to protect them, that reality could be closer than we think. Dr Coco Parkinson-Huggins Researcher , Theos

article_text:
Films and events

Galas

La Bola Negra

A genre-defying queer epic, rooted in the legacy of beloved writer Federico García Lorca, this is majestic and original filmmaking.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Directors Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo

Screenwriters Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi, Alberto Conejero

With Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Penélope Cruz

Spain-France 2026. 155min

Courtesy of Altitude

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

Spain, 1932. A young man awaits to see if he has secured membership of the local casino. In 1937, a young nationalist soldier guards a republican prisoner. Jump to 2017 and an unexpected document is inherited by an historian from his grandfather. These timelines and a breathtaking cinematic audacity shapes this dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych about communication, inheritance, silence and memory.

Maria Delgado

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Bunker

Set against a backdrop of widening class divisions and capitalist excess, Florian Zeller’s elegantly crafted psychological thriller is anchored by magnificent performances from Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

The Beloved

Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.

The Man I Love

Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.

article_text:
全国の美術館や博物館などのグッズが一堂に会するイベント「美術展ナビフェス2026」を9月29日、東京・大手町のよみうり大手町小ホールで開催しました。

前回の全ブース紹介では、今年の新規出展館を紹介しました。

今回は会場で見つけた個性豊かなグッズの数々を紹介します。さっそくブースをのぞいてみましょう。（※商品はタイミングにより品切れの場合がございます）

静岡県立美術館

昨年の美術展ナビフェスでは、伊藤若冲『樹花鳥獣図屛風』 右隻に描かれた白象 のぬいぐるみ 「じゅかぞう（伊藤若冲の象さんマスコット）」が大人気でした。どうやら今年は新メンバーがいるとのウワサ…。

左隻に描かれた鳳凰が 飛び出してきました。その名も「じゅかちょう（伊藤若冲の鳳凰さんマスコット）」です！この「じゅがちょう」、パーツごとに素材が違っていたり、作り込みがすごい。ぜひ「じゅかぞう」と「じゅかちょう」セットでお迎えしてみてはいかがでしょうか。

静岡ゆかりの画家・ 石田徹也 の作品をモチーフにしたグッズもありました。 同館が石田徹也作品をグッズ化するのはこれらが初めて とのこと。トートバッグの裏面にはスケッチがプリントされ、アクセントにビニールポケットが付くなど凝っています。

静岡県立美術館 のグッズはこちら▶

国立能楽堂

国立能楽堂のブースでは、グッズの制作担当の方とお話しすることができました。じわじわ人気が出てきている国立能楽堂のキャラクター「はんにゃちゃん」。 藁 人形とはんにゃちゃんという組み合わせがインパクト大のアンブレラマーカーは、絵柄の検討段階では演目に関係した柄がいくつか候補にあったそうですが、最終的には能の演目に全く登場しない藁人形が選ばれたとのこと（笑）。

最近の売れ筋は、能絵があしらわれたおしゃれなグッズたち。 ヘアアクセサリーを スカーフの留め具として使用するなど、さまざまな使い方が提案されていました。

国立能楽堂 のグッズはこちら▶

国立劇場

昨年の美術展ナビフェスで登場し、人気を博した「くろごちゃんもちころりん」。なんと今年は新色が登場！「新色はかわいい水色と白ね♪」と思っていましたが、ブースで話を聞いてみると、実際の舞台で黒子は波などのシーンでは水色を、雪のシーンでは白の衣装を着ているそうです。くろごちゃんをきっかけに、伝統芸能の知識がひとつ増えました。歌舞伎を見に行ったら、舞台の演出を陰ながら支える黒子にも注目です。

国立劇場 のグッズはこちら▶

奈良国立博物館

正倉院やざんまいず、アウトドアブランド「mont-bell」とのコラボグッズなど、ブースには魅力的なグッズがたくさんならんでいましたが、「これは！昔からあります！」とブースの方々が口をそろえておすすめするのは「元気が出る仏像」シリーズ。奈良を訪れた修学旅行生にも根強い人気があるそうです。

釈迦、天人、地蔵菩薩、蔵王権現、阿修羅、走り大黒など、 動きのある仏像 がPOPな色とかわいいデザインで描かれています。眺めていると、なんだか元気が出てきました！

奈良国立博物館 のグッズはこちら▶

九州国立博物館

「埴輪鹿」の大胆なダイカットのトートバッグで人々の注目を集めていたのは、九州国立博物館のブースです。ブースの方によると、脚の部分は水筒を入れるのにぴったりで、A4サイズのファイルもギリギリ入るとのこと。普段使いとしても（？）便利なサイズ感です。

見てください、このこだわり！バッグの裏側には「埴輪鹿」の後ろ姿がプリントされています。

九州国立博物館 のグッズはこちら▶

静嘉堂＠丸の内

漫画『極主夫道』に登場し一躍話題になった「ぷっくりシール 」が並ぶのは静嘉堂＠丸の内のブースです。（漫画『極主夫道』の作者、おおのこうすけ先生に書面でインタビューした記事は こちら 。）

こちらは静嘉堂が誇る国宝《曜変天目》のぷっくりシール。シールの特徴である立体感とツヤは、うつわとの相性抜群です。

古代中国の墓を守るためにつくられた「加彩鎮墓獣(人面)」をモチーフにしたアクリル御守りなど、ユニークなグッズもありました。

静嘉堂＠丸の内 のグッズはこちら▶

町田市立国際版画美術館

巨大な「あやつり人形」で今年の美術展ナビフェスを大いに盛り上げてくれたのは、町田市立国際版画美術館のブースです。「あやつり人形」は 糸を引くと手足がパタパタと滑稽に動く仕組みの人形で、 通常サイズは美術展ナビオンラインストアで販売中です。自分で切り取って組み立てる商品なので、工作好きな方におすすめ。作業に没頭できます。

町田市立国際版画美術館は近所の町工場の方々とグッズの開発を行っているそうで、驚くべきはそのスピード。町工場の方が企画展の内覧会や開幕日に展覧会を訪れ、「この作品でグッズを作ろう！」と決めると、展覧会会期中にそのグッズがショップに並ぶそうです。

ほかにも 「きせかえ人形」や、 本をめくるとしおりが立ち上がる「月岡芳年 美人しおり」など、楽しいグッズがたくさんありました。

町田市立国際版画美術館 のグッズはこちら▶

article_text:
Nach dem überraschenden Tod des US-amerikanischen Künstlers Lucien Smith steht nun die Todesursache fest: Der 37-Jährige starb an einer Überdosis Fentanyl und Oxycodon

Das teilte das New Yorker Institut für Rechtsmedizin mit. Der Tod des 37-Jährigen, der am 7. September leblos in seiner Wohnung in Manhattan gefunden worden war , wurde als Unfall eingestuft.

Bekannt wurde Smith vor allem durch seine "Rain Paintings", für die er verdünnte Farbe mit einem Feuerlöscher auf große, ungrundierte Leinwände sprühte. Die Arbeiten machten ihn zu einem Star des Kunstmarkts. 2013 erzielte ein Gemälde aus seiner Abschlussausstellung bei Phillips 389.000 Dollar – Smith war damals 24 Jahre alt. 2014 wurden Arbeiten des Künstlers bei Auktionen für insgesamt mehr als vier Millionen Dollar umgesetzt.

Kurz vor seinem Tod hatte der Künstler eine neue Serie von vier "Rain Paintings" auf einem verlassenen Baseballfeld in Montauk auf Long Island geschaffen, berichtet die "New York Times" . Dafür habe er eine Sprühvorrichtung mit einem Kompressor errichtet, die seine bisherige Technik mit Feuerlöschern ablöste. Die Arbeiten sind derzeit in der Ausstellung "Delay of Game" in der Tripoli Gallery in Wainscott zu sehen, die noch bis zum 23. November läuft. Es war Smiths erste Zusammenarbeit mit einer Galerie seit zwölf Jahren.

In den Wochen vor seinem Tod habe Smith mit psychischen Problemen zu kämpfen. Textnachrichten, die der "New York Times" von seinem Freund Bill Powers, dem Gründer der Half Gallery, zur Verfügung gestellt wurden, zeigten, dass der Künstler von Angstattacken, Erschöpfung und einem persönlichen Tiefpunkt berichtete. Ende August, wenige Tage vor seinem Tod, sei er fünf Tage abstinent gewesen, sagte Powers der Zeitung. Er habe Smith als eine Art Sohn betrachtet.

Smith hatte im vergangenen Jahr gemeinsam mit dem Koch Mathieu Canet das Restaurant FOOD in Manhattans Chinatown eröffnet. Nach seinem Tod versammelten sich dort Freunde und Weggefährten zu einer provisorischen Gedenkstätte. Eine weitere Gedenkfeier fand in Montauk statt, wo der Künstler lebte und arbeitete.

article_text:
Through painting, photography and personal archives, Sudanese artist Salah Elmur explores the fragile relationship between memory, displacement and belonging in ‘Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone ‘ at Jameel Arts Centre, Dubai.

How do we remember a homeland transformed by distance, conflict and the passage of time? In ‘Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone ‘ , Sudanese artist Salah Elmur examines the enduring relationship between personal memory and collective history. Bringing together paintings, archival photographs, sketches and ephemera, the exhibition traces his evolving connection to Sudan amid political upheaval and displacement.

Drawing on childhood memories of life near the Blue Nile, Elmur constructs richly layered compositions in which everyday encounters, agricultural landscapes and familial histories intersect with myth and imagination. Central to his practice is the photographic archive of Studio Kamal, his family’s Khartoum studio. By reinterpreting these images through painting, Elmur questions how identities are preserved, transformed and reconstructed across generations.

Curated by Zain Al Saie and Qutouf Elobaid, the exhibition unfolds across three chapters, To Appear Otherwise , Salt of the Earth and Mourning Song , exploring family, labour, grief and belonging. Through Elmur’s distinctive visual language, memory emerges not as a fixed record of the past, but as an evolving space through which histories of Sudan continue to be imagined, questioned and reclaimed.

This exhibition is on view at the Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai until 14 March 2027
